AL.board: Alabama Board of Medical Examiners & Medical Licensure Commission
AL.due: Fixed date: all licenses expire annually on December 31, regardless of when issued. Renewal window is October 1 through December 31 via the Licensee Gateway.
AL.fee: $300 (full MD/DO license, annual renewal). ACSC (Alabama Controlled Substances Certificate) renewal is a separate $150 if held.

AK.board: Alaska State Medical Board (Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing, Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development)
AK.due: All medical licenses expire December 31 of even-numbered years, regardless of issuance date. Current cycle: January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026. Licenses issued within 90 days of the expiration date are issued to the next biennial expiration date. One renewal notice is sent by email or mail at least 30 days before expiration, usually in late October.
AK.fee: $350 (active MD or DO, full-term biennial renewal, or lapsed less than 1 year). $175 prorated if the license was first issued in the second year of the cycle. Inactive status: $200 full-term or $100 prorated. Retired status: $150 one time.

AZ.due: MD: every other year on or before the licensee's birthday (A.R.S. 32-1430(A); the on-year depends on your license record, check your profile at azmd.gov Doctor Search). DO: December 31 of either even-numbered or odd-numbered years depending on the licensee's assigned renew-by date; the DO renewal portal opens on or about October 1.
AZ.fee: $500 (MD active license, 2-year renewal). DO: $636 biennial, non-refundable.

AR.due: Annually on or before the last day of the licensee's birth month. Board language: "Your medical license, if granted, must be renewed annually on or before the last day of your birth month. There is no grace period." Email reminders go out about 60, 45, and 30 days before the end of the birth month; failure to receive notice is not an excuse.
AR.fee: $11 (MD/DO annual renewal, per the ASMB fee schedule PDF reflecting the Act 114 of 2023 fee reduction stated to run 7/1/2023 through 6/30/2026). Statutory default is $70 per year under A.C.A. 17-95-411(a)(4), which is the cap; the board may keep fees reduced in future years but the schedule says fees are subject to change without notice. Waived for active-duty military.

CA.due: MD: license expires at 11:59 p.m. on the last day of the month in which the license was originally issued, every two years (not birth month). Initial MD licenses issued on or after January 1, 2024 get a 26-month first cycle, then revert to 24 months. DO: biennial cycle renewed through BreEZe; OMBC's loaded pages state the two-year period runs between the prior and current expiration dates but do not explicitly publish the anchor rule (issuance month vs other), so that detail is left unstated rather than guessed.
CA.fee: MD active: $1,206 total ($1,151 base plus mandatory $25 Steven M. Thompson Physician Corps Loan Repayment fee plus $30 CURES fee). DO active: $455 (includes $25 per B&P Code 2436.5 and $30 CURES per B&P Code 208); DO inactive: $325 (includes the $25 fee, no CURES)

CO.board: Colorado Medical Board (Department of Regulatory Agencies, Division of Professions and Occupations)
CO.due: All Physician and Pro Bono Physician licenses expire on April 30 of odd-numbered years, regardless of when the license was issued (next expiration: April 30, 2027). Renewal opens in the DPO Online Services portal approximately 4 to 6 weeks before the expiration date (the Applications page says renewals open about 4-5 weeks prior; the DPO FAQ says the renewal link appears when the license is within 6 weeks of expiration).

CT.board: Connecticut Department of Public Health, Practitioner Licensing and Investigations Section (adjudicative board: Connecticut Medical Examining Board)
CT.due: Annually during the licensee's birth month. Per DPH, "Most licenses expire in the first birth month following issuance and are renewable annually thereafter"; Conn. Gen. Stat. 19a-88(b) requires each person licensed to practice medicine or surgery to register "annually, during the month of such person's birth."
CT.fee: $575 per year (Physician/Surgeon, MD or DO). Statutory composition under CGS 19a-88(b): the class I professional services fee plus $5, plus an additional $5 for medicine/surgery licensees. DPH's Physician Licensure page lists the renewal fee as $575.00. Paid online by credit card or electronic funds transfer.

DE.board: Delaware Board of Medical Licensure and Discipline (Division of Professional Regulation)
DE.due: All physician licenses expire March 31 of odd-numbered years (next: March 31, 2027). A renewal notice is emailed to the address on record a few months before expiration.

DC.board: District of Columbia Board of Medicine (DC Health, Health Regulation and Licensing Administration)
DC.due: Last day of the licensee's birth month, in odd or even years matching the licensee's birth year. Board statement: all credentials issued or renewed on or after June 16, 2024 "will expire on the last day of the holder's birth month," and "if your birthday is in an odd year, your future renewals will occur in odd years (and the same for even years)." This replaced the old fixed December 31 of even-numbered years anchor; licenses renewed before June 16, 2024 kept their existing expiration for that term and convert at their next renewal.
DC.fee: $500 (MD/DO renewal license fee for the 2-year term, per 17 DCMR 3500.1, Medical Doctors: "License (original, renewal, temporary, renewal, or reinstated) - By endorsement, reciprocity, renewal, waiver... $500.00"). A $50 criminal background check fee also appears in the same schedule and the Board notes CBC review is part of renewal processing.

FL.board: Florida Board of Medicine (Florida Department of Health, Division of Medical Quality Assurance)
FL.due: MD: fixed date, January 31. The board splits MD licensees into two groups: "licenses in Group 1 expire on January 31 in even-numbered years and those in Group 2 expire on January 31 in odd-numbered years" (your group is set by the board, not by your birth date or license anniversary; check your printed expiration date). DO: fixed date, the licensure biennial period concludes on March 31 of even-numbered years (all DOs renew together). Online renewal opens no later than 90 days before expiration; the deadline is midnight Eastern Time on the expiration date.
FL.fee: MD active-to-active: $355.00. DO active-to-active: $405.00. Both boards add a $43.25 FDLE fingerprint-retention fee at renewal if your fingerprint retention is expiring, and $100.00 if you hold a dispensing-practitioner registration. Other on-time statuses, MD: inactive-to-inactive $125, active-to-inactive $475, inactive-to-active $605, to-retired $55. DO: inactive-to-inactive $205, active-to-inactive $205, inactive-to-active $605, to-retired $55.

GA.due: Last day of the licensee's birth month, every two years. Rule 360-2-.05: all active licenses must be renewed biennially by the last day of the month in which the applicant's birthday falls, and the license expires at the end of that birth month.
GA.fee: $230 (full physician license, 2-year renewal; same $230 for Administrative, Institutional, and Telemedicine physician licenses; Provisional is $50)

HI.board: Hawaii Medical Board (Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs, Professional and Vocational Licensing Division)
HI.due: MD: January 31 of every even-numbered year, regardless of when the license was issued (current period February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2028). DO: June 30 of every even-numbered year (current period July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028). Government-employed physicians (MDG) renew annually by January 31 of every year.
HI.fee: $402.00 (Physician MD, on-time 2-year renewal, as posted by the board for the Feb 1, 2026 to Jan 31, 2028 period). Osteopathic Physician (DOS): $312.00. Physician-Government (MDG, annual): $171.00.

ID.board: Idaho State Board of Medicine (Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses, DOPL)
ID.due: Licensee's birthdate. As of April 1, 2026, DOPL began transitioning the Board of Medicine to biennial licenses that expire on the licensee's birthday, phased in by odd/even birth year so renewals spread across two cycles. Before this transition, DOPL licenses renewed on a June cycle (1-year or 2-year licenses in the month of June). Renewal can be completed up to 60 days before the birthday expiration. Physicians mid-transition should confirm their individual expiration date in the eDOPL portal.
ID.fee: $160 per year for both Physician and Surgeon (MD) and Osteopathic Physician and Surgeon (DO), effective January 1, 2025 (reduced from $200). DOPL states biennial renewals are charged only for whole years, so a 2-year renewal doubles the annual fee, but the board has not published a single biennial dollar figure.

IL.board: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR), Division of Professional Regulation
IL.due: Fixed date: all Physician and Surgeon licenses expire July 31 every third year (68 Ill. Adm. Code 1285.120: "every license issued under the Medical Practice Act of 1987 shall expire on July 31, 1990, and every third year thereafter", so 2026, 2029, 2032). One-time exception: the 2026 renewal deadline was extended to August 31, 2026 by an IDFPR variance dated 7-20-2026, due to the Department's transition to new data and operating systems.
IL.fee: $543 for the 3-year renewal if the licensee has held the Illinois Physician and Surgeon license for more than 365 days as of the application signature date; $181 if held for 365 days or fewer (first renewal shortly after initial licensure). Same license type and fees for MD and DO. Source: IDFPR 2026 Physicians Batch Renewal Form IL486-2611 (4/26).

IN.board: Indiana Medical Licensing Board (Indiana Professional Licensing Agency)
IN.due: All physician (MD and DO) licenses expire at 11:59 p.m. EDT on October 31 of odd-numbered years, statewide, regardless of issue date. The most recent cycle closed 10/31/2025; the next renewal deadline is 10/31/2027. Renewal notices are emailed approximately 90 days before expiration to the email address on file.
IN.fee: $200 (active MD or DO, 2-year renewal). $100 for renewal into Inactive status (no office or practice permitted). CSR (Controlled Substance Registration) is a separate renewal with its own fee.

IA.board: Iowa Board of Medicine (Department of Inspections, Appeals, and Licensing)
IA.due: License expires on the first day of the licensee's birth month; renewal issues a two-year license that again expires on the first day of the birth month (Iowa Admin. Code r. 481-652.12(3)). Online renewal opens no more than 60 days before the renewal date.
IA.fee: $450 if renewed online, $550 if renewed by paper application, per biennial period (prorated if the current license was issued for less than 24 months); $0 for physicians on active duty in the U.S. armed forces, reserves, or national guard during the renewal period. A $7 online transaction fee applies to online purchases (Iowa Admin. Code r. 481-651.4(1)c, 481-651.1).

KS.board: Kansas State Board of Healing Arts (KSBHA)
KS.due: Fixed calendar dates by license type, not birth month. MD: all Medical Doctor licenses expire July 31; the renewal cycle runs May 15 through July 31 each year, with on-time renewal due by June 30 and July 1 to July 31 as the late-renewal window. DO: all Osteopathic Doctor licenses expire October 31; renewal cycle August 15 through October 31, on-time by September 30, late window October 1 to October 31.
KS.fee: $360 online ($430 by paper) for annual renewal of an active or federally active MD/DO license under the Healing Arts Act; inactive or exempt license renews at $150; resident active $100; reentry active $300

KY.due: Fixed date for all licensees: renewal is due by March 1 of each year. Reminder notices are mailed to all active licensees in late December. Renewals paid after March 1 but before April 1 require a penalty fee; failure to renew by April 1 makes the license automatically inactive.
KY.fee: $150 (annual registration or renewal of regular MD/DO license, online). Paper renewal adds $10. Limited license renewal is $65.

LA.board: Louisiana State Board of Medical Examiners (LSBME)
LA.due: License expires annually on the first day of the month in which the licensee was born (LAC 46:XLV.415: every license "shall annually expire... on the first day of the month in which the licensee was born"). Renewal must be filed on or before that date; the online window opens only 56 days before expiration.
LA.fee: $332 per year (active MD/DO): $300 renewal fee plus $25 physician health program assessment plus $7 CME assessment under La. R.S. 37:1281. Derived from statute; the board site itself publishes only the $382 initial licensure fee (which is the same $350 + $25 + $7 statutory structure). Reduced by one half for qualifying physicians age 70+ or disabled who have surrendered CDS registration (LAC 46:XLV.418).

ME.board: Maine Board of Licensure in Medicine
ME.due: Last day of the licensee's birth month, in even or odd years matching the licensee's birth year: physicians born in an even-numbered year expire on the last day of their birth month in an even-numbered year, those born in an odd-numbered year in an odd-numbered year (MD board FAQ). The DO board also sets the renewal date by date of birth per its application instructions; the DO statute (32 MRS 2581-1) leaves the exact schedule to board rule.
ME.fee: $500 (MD active license, 2-year renewal). DO: $525 biennial renewal; $0 for DOs age 70+ (CME still required). Initial licenses expiring within 6 months of issuance renew at a prorated $150 (MD).

MD.due: Licenses expire September 30 in alternating years by last name: A-L expire in even years (renewal window July 15 to September 30, 2026, 11:59 pm EST), M-Z in odd years. Not tied to birth month.
MD.fee: $512.00 total for MDs and DOs (2026 cycle): $436 renewal fee + $50 rehabilitation/peer review program + $26 Maryland Health Care Commission assessment (Health Occ. sec. 1-209). IMLC compact-licensed physicians pay an additional $25 Compact processing fee ($537 total, paid to the Compact).

MA.board: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Medicine (BORIM)
MA.due: Birth date. Board states: renewal of a full medical license occurs on the first birth date after license issuance, unless the birthday falls within 90 days of obtaining the initial license, in which case the first renewal moves to the following birth date. Renewals thereafter run on a two-year birth date cycle.
MA.fee: $600 (Physician full license renewal, biennial; administrative and volunteer licenses also $600)

MI.board: Michigan Board of Medicine (Bureau of Professional Licensing, Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs)
MI.due: License-specific: medicine and osteopathic medicine licenses expire triennially on the anniversary of the license issue date (R 338.7002, Public Health Code General Rules). LARA states expiration dates vary and to check the date printed on the license. Online renewal in MiPLUS opens no sooner than 90 days before the expiration date.
MI.fee: $314.40 (MD or DO 3-year renewal, per LARA License Renewal Fees schedule and the DO licensing guide rev. 1/26/2026). Controlled substance license renewal is a separate $248.10 if applicable. Payment by Visa, Mastercard, American Express, or Discover only. Note: the MD licensing guide web page states $314.00, which conflicts with the fee schedule; see notes.

MN.due: Annual cycle ending on the last day of the licensee's month of birth (Minnesota Rules 5600.0605, subp. 4: renewal cycles "begin on the last day of the month of the licensee's birth"). Online renewal opens on the first day of the 2nd month before expiration; example given by the board: a license expiring June 30 can be renewed online starting May 1.
MN.fee: $192 (Physician Annual License, MD and DO; confirmed in Minn. Stat. 147.01 subd. 7 as "physician annual registration renewal fee, $192" and in the board's September 2, 2025 fee schedule PDF)

MS.board: Mississippi State Board of Medical Licensure (MSBML)
MS.due: Fixed statewide window: renewal opens May 1 and the deadline is June 30 each year, for every permanent MD/DO license. The renewal year runs July 1 to June 30. Late renewal begins August 1.
MS.fee: $300.00 (MD/DO permanent license, 1-year renewal) plus a convenience fee charged through MELS

MO.board: Missouri State Board of Registration for the Healing Arts
MO.due: Fixed date: all physician licenses expire January 31 of every year. Renewal information is mailed and/or emailed on or before December 1. A renewal is timely if the fee is received before expiration; forms postmarked February 1 or after are delinquent, except that when January 31 falls on a weekend or legal holiday, a postmark on the next business day is not delinquent (20 CSR 2150-2.001(17)).
MO.fee: $147 (Permanent Physician Renewal Fee, MD and DO alike, 1-year registration) per 20 CSR 2150-2.080(1)(A)4. All fees are nonrefundable.

MT.board: Montana Board of Medical Examiners (Department of Labor and Industry, Professional Licensing Bureau)
MT.due: Licenses expire March 31 of the expiration year. Physicians (MDs and osteopaths) renew online between February 1 and March 31 of their renewal year (board renewal-process and license-information pages; ARM 24.101.413 table lists "Physician, Biennially, March 31"). The board does not publish whether an individual's renewal year is even or odd; it is set per license.
MT.fee: $375 (active physician, 2-year renewal) per the board FAQ, plus the Montana Prescription Drug Registry fee of $30/year ($60 for a two-year renewal) for physicians with prescribing authority. Inactive renewal: $190. Note: ARM 24.156.409 (rules PDF current through 3/31/24) itemizes the $190 inactive renewal but routes the active renewal fee to the department's standardized fee rule ARM 24.101.403; the $375 active figure comes from the board's own FAQ.

NE.board: Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services, Division of Public Health, Licensure Unit (Board of Medicine and Surgery)
NE.due: All physician and osteopathic physician licenses expire October 1 of every even-numbered year, regardless of when the license was issued. Renewal application and fee must be postmarked (or submitted online) on or before October 1 of the even year. Next expiration: October 1, 2026.
NE.fee: $171 total for active status: $121 renewal fee plus a $50 Patient Safety Cash Fund fee (the $50 cannot be waived). Active-Military status: $50 (Patient Safety Cash Fund fee only). Inactive status: $0.

NV.board: Nevada State Board of Medical Examiners
NV.due: MD: biennial registration due on or before June 30 of each odd-numbered year (or next business day if June 30 falls on a weekend or holiday), per NRS 630.267; the current registration period runs July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2027, so the next MD renewal is due June 30, 2027. DO: renewal due on or before December 31 (NRS 633.471); per the board's Summer 2025 newsletter, the last annual deadline was December 31, 2025, and starting in 2026 DO licenses renew in every even-numbered year for a two-year period, making December 31, 2026 the next DO renewal deadline.
NV.fee: MD: $750 biennial registration for an active MD ($375 inactive; $375 if renewing for only the second half of the biennium), per the board's Licensure Fees schedule; statutory cap is $1,000 (NRS 630.268). DO: $350 renewal fee ($200 inactive) on the fee schedule effective July 1, 2023; the board's Summer 2025 newsletter states DO renewal fees will increase effective with the first biennial renewal, with the revised chart to be posted (statutory cap for the biennial DO renewal fee is $1,000, NRS 633.501). A 2.5% card-processing fee applies to MD-board credit card payments.

NH.board: New Hampshire Board of Medicine (under the Office of Professional Licensure and Certification, OPLC)
NH.due: License anniversary: under RSA 310:8, II, "Licenses issued by the office shall be valid for 2 years from the date of issuance." The completed renewal application, fee, and supporting documents must be filed on or before the expiration of the license (RSA 310:8, III). OPLC must send renewal notice at least 2 months before expiration (RSA 310:8, IV), and the OPLC renewal page says licensees get an email renewal notification 90 days before expiration.
NH.fee: $413.00 (Physician/Administrative Physician renewal, per the OPLC Board of Medicine fee page; includes the mandatory $28.00 Professional Health Program fee). Compact Physician renewal is also $413.00.

NJ.board: New Jersey State Board of Medical Examiners (Division of Consumer Affairs)
NJ.due: Fixed date: all MD and DO licenses expire June 30 of ODD-numbered years, regardless of when the license was issued. The board's licensing presentation states renewal is "Every 2 years on odd years" for MD and DO (example cycle: July 1, 2005 to June 30, 2007), and the DCA's own license verification system shows current MD licenses expiring 6/30/2027. Renewal notices are mailed at least 60 days before expiration (N.J.S.A. 45:1-7.1(e)).
NJ.fee: $580 (active MD/DO, full biennial renewal). The board FAQ states the registration fee is $290 per year of the biennial period; the board's licensing presentation lists renewal fees as: Active $580; Reduced-fee active-retired (65+, no HMO or hospital affiliation) $125; Inactive $0; Retired $0. Dollar figures come from the board's 2017 presentation and the FAQ (last modified 2023); the governing fee rule N.J.A.C. 13:35-6.13 publishes its table only as an image, so the current codified amounts could not be read directly.

NM.due: On or before July 1 of every third year (NMSA 1978 Section 61-6-26). Licenses expire July 1; online renewal must be completed by June 30. Renewal opens about 3 months before expiration. Initial licenses are issued for no more than 13 months and no less than 1 month, expiring the following July 1, which places the new licensee into the triennial cycle.
NM.fee: $600 total (active physician triennial renewal: $450 renewal fee plus $150 impaired physicians program fee, 16.10.9.8(B) NMAC). Statutory caps: renewal not to exceed $500 plus impaired physician fee not to exceed $150 per 3-year period (NMSA 61-6-19). Telemedicine license triennial renewal is $400.

NY.board: New York State Education Department, Office of the Professions (State Board for Medicine)
NY.due: Rolling per-licensee registration period: NY Education Law 6502 has the Department establish the beginning date of each licensee's registration period, so the two-year cycle runs from your own registration date, not a birth month or fixed statewide date. NYSED mails a Registration Renewal Document with a PIN approximately four months before the registration expires (per the Office of the Professions FAQ). Physicians and medical physicists are on two-year periods; most other NY professions are three-year.
NY.fee: $600 (registration renewal for Medicine, MD and DO, per two-year registration period; Office of the Professions Fees Chart, Rev. 2/21). Online payment is credit card only (Visa, MasterCard, American Express) and fees are not refundable.

NC.due: Every year, no later than 30 days after the licensee's birthday, regardless of license issue date (N.C. Gen. Stat. 90-13.2). A licensee's first renewal is due within 30 days of their NEXT birthday, even if that birthday falls shortly after the license was issued.
NC.fee: $250 (MD and DO, annual renewal; set by N.C. Gen. Stat. 90-13.2 and the board's Renewal Fees schedule, last updated 12.30.2025)

ND.due: Licenses expire on the physician's birthday every other year (effective August 1, 2023). A new license first expires the second time the birthday comes around after Board approval. The online renewal window opens 59 days before the expiration date; email reminders go out 59 and 14 days before expiration.
ND.fee: $405.00 online renewal for a two-year license (board renewal page, effective August 1, 2023). Underlying rule sets licensure at $200 per year (N.D. Admin. Code 50-02-07.1-01); the extra $5 appears to be an online processing charge, which the board does not itemize.

OH.due: Individual expiration date: per ORC 4731.281, "A license shall expire on the date that is two years from the date of issuance and may be renewed for additional two-year periods." Not tied to birth month or a fixed statewide date. Renewal can be submitted within 180 days before the expiration date (board renewal page).
OH.fee: $305 (MD/DO/DPM biennial renewal, per ORC 4731.281 and the board's fee list), of which $20 goes to the Ohio Physician Loan Repayment Fund; plus a $3.50 eLicense transaction fee, paid online by credit card

OK.board: Oklahoma State Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision
OK.due: MD: annual reregistration during the month of initial licensure, per OAC 435:10-7-10 ("Reregistration shall be conducted during the month of initial licensure of each individual licensee"). It is NOT birth month and NOT a fixed calendar date. DO: all osteopathic licenses expire June 30 every year; the OSBOE renewal window opens May 1.
OK.fee: MD: $200 (application for annual reregistration fee, full medical license, OAC 435:1-1-7). DO: $250 annually (OSBOE FAQ and fee rule OAC 510:10-7).

OR.due: Fixed date, statewide: the renewal application and fee must be received and satisfactorily complete on or before December 31 of each odd-numbered year for all physicians and physician associates (OAR 847-008-0005(1)). All MD/DO licensees share the same deadline regardless of when the license was issued; the current registration period ends December 31, 2027. Emeritus renews by December 31 every year; acupuncturists (also under this board) renew by June 30 of even-numbered years.
OR.fee: $756 total for an Active MD/DO two-year renewal per the board fee schedule effective 7/2/2026: $608 license registration + $20 OHSU library + $50 HPSP fee + $70 prescription monitoring + $8 OHA workforce database. Inactive or Administrative Medicine status totals $686 (no PDMP fee). Active-One Year (postgraduate) is $378/year; Emeritus $114/year. Underlying rule: registration is $314/year including $10/year OHSU library (OAR 847-005-0005), rising to $375/year on or after March 1, 2028. All fees are nonrefundable, nontransferable, and cannot be prorated.

PA.board: Pennsylvania State Board of Medicine (Bureau of Professional and Occupational Affairs, Department of State)
PA.due: Fixed dates in even-numbered years, and the two boards differ: MD licenses expire December 31 of every even-numbered year (except MD Training licenses); DO licenses expire October 31 of every even-numbered year. Current cycle ends 10/31/2026 (DO) and 12/31/2026 (MD). Renewal opens in PALS approximately 60 days before expiration.
PA.fee: $360 (MD unrestricted license, 2-year renewal, 49 Pa. Code 16.13); $450 (DO unrestricted license, 2-year renewal, 49 Pa. Code 25.231, rate effective for the Nov 1, 2024 to Oct 31, 2026 biennium and thereafter). IMLC compact renewals add a $25.00 IMLC fee paid through imlcc.com.

RI.board: Rhode Island Board of Medical Licensure and Discipline (Rhode Island Department of Health)
RI.due: Fixed statewide date, not tied to birth month or issue anniversary. Per 216-RICR-40-05-1.5.6(A), licenses "expire biennially on the first (1st) day of July of the next even-numbered year," i.e. the license runs through June 30 of the even year. The renewal application and fee must be filed before July 1 of each even-numbered year, with payment postmarked on or before July 1 (1.5.6(B)); RIGL 5-37-10 sets the application submission at on or before June 1, with the new certificate effective July 1 and expiring June 30 two years later.
RI.fee: $1,090.00 (biennial renewal, same for MD and DO); $870.00 for "Renewal with Approved Training" (per 216-RICR-10-05-2 § 2.9, citing RIGL 5-37-10(a) and 23-1-54)

SC.board: South Carolina Board of Medical Examiners (SC Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation)
SC.due: Fixed statewide date: licenses expire June 30 of odd-numbered years (current cycle is 2025-2027; the prior license lapsed June 30, 2025 if not renewed, per the board's 2025-2027 late renewal application). SC Code 40-47-41 provides that a license "may be renewed biennially or as otherwise provided by the board." The board page does not publish the exact opening date of the on-time renewal window for MD/DO.

SD.board: South Dakota Board of Medical and Osteopathic Examiners
SD.due: Fixed common date: all physician licenses must be renewed on or before March 1 of odd-numbered years (SDCL 36-4-24.2). The online renewal opens 90 days before expiration (ARSD 20:47:03:13), i.e. around December 1 of the preceding even-numbered year.
SD.fee: $400 (biennial renewal of the physician and surgeon license, MD and DO alike; ARSD 20:47:06:01, within the $400 statutory cap of SDCL 36-4-24.1)

TN.board: Tennessee Board of Medical Examiners (Tennessee Department of Health)
TN.due: Birth month. Rule 0880-02-.09(1)(a) (identical for DOs in 1050-02-.07): the due date is the license expiration date, which is the last day of the month in which the license holder's birthday falls, under the Division of Health Related Boards biennial birthdate renewal system (Rule 1200-10-1-.10). The board site states everyone renews every two years in their birth month, with the renewal year keyed to birth year (even birth years renew in even years, odd in odd). Online renewal opens 60 days before expiration; renewal notices go out roughly 90 days ahead (paper, or email for opted-in licensees).
TN.fee: MD: $300 Licensure Renewal Fee plus $10 biennial State Regulatory Fee, so $310 total per 2-year cycle (Rule 0880-02-.02(1)(f) and (g), June 2025 revision). DO: $200 Licensure Renewal Fee plus $10 biennial State Regulatory Fee, so $210 total per 2-year cycle (Rule 1050-02-.02(1)(b) and (c), December 2025 revision).

TX.due: Fixed quarterly dates assigned by TMB at licensure. Board text: "Physician licenses expire at one of 4 times during the year; February 28th, May 31st, August 31st, or November 30th." The year is set by license-number parity: "Even number licenses expire in even number years and odd number licenses expire in odd number years." Initial registration is pro-rated (12-month $281.48 or 24-month $467.48) to land the license on its assigned cycle.
TX.fee: $491.48 (biennial physician registration, as of 9/1/2025): Agency fee $370.00 + SB 104 fee $80.00 + Office of Patient Protection $2.00 + NPDB $21.00 + Texas Physician Health Program $7.00 + PMP $11.48. Paper renewal adds a $50 surcharge when online renewal is available; credit card payment adds a Texas.gov processing fee (electronic check does not).

UT.board: Utah Division of Professional Licensing (DOPL), Physicians Licensing Board
UT.due: MD: "Physician licenses expire on January 31 of even years." DO: "Osteopathic Physician and Surgeon license renewals are due May 31st of even years." Controlled substance licenses renew at the same time as the main license. (Next renewal for both: 2028, since the 2026 dates have passed.)
UT.fee: $193 (MD or DO, 2-year renewal). Add $78 to renew a Utah controlled substance license (total $271). Verified on the FY 7/1/2025-6/30/2026 DOPL fee schedule ("Physician and Surgeon ... Renewal Fee 193.00"; "Osteopathic Physician and Surgeon 200.00 / 193.00"; "Controlled Substance 100.00 / 78.00") and stated as "$193 renewal fee" on the DO renewal page. Fees are non-refundable and "subject to change each July 1."

VT.board: Vermont Board of Medical Practice (Vermont Department of Health)
VT.due: MD: licenses expire November 30 of even-numbered years (next deadline November 30, 2026); a license issued before September 1 of an even year expires that same November 30 and must be renewed at the full fee. DO: licenses renew September 30 of even-numbered years per the OPR fee and renewal-date schedule (next deadline September 30, 2026).
VT.fee: MD: $525 biennial renewal (26 V.S.A. § 1401a(a)(2); at least $25 of it funds the Vermont Practitioner Recovery Network). DO: $350 biennial renewal (OPR fee schedule, updated 7/1/2025).

VA.board: Virginia Board of Medicine (Department of Health Professions)
VA.due: During the licensee's birth month in each even-numbered year. 18VAC85-20-230(A) requires renewal "biennially during his birth month," and the fee regulation 18VAC85-20-22 sets the medicine/osteopathic medicine renewal fee as due in the licensee's birth month in each even-numbered year.
VA.fee: $337 (active MD/DO biennial renewal; inactive license renewal is $168) per 18VAC85-20-22

WA.due: MD: "Licenses must be renewed every two years on the practitioner's birthday" (WAC 246-919-990; postgraduate limited licenses renew annually on program dates). DO: licenses must be renewed every year on the physician's birthday (WAC 246-853-990).
WA.fee: MD active 2-year renewal: $996 total = $824 base renewal + $32 UW HEAL-WA online access surcharge + $140 Washington Physician Health Program surcharge (RCW 18.71.310(2)). DO active 1-year renewal: $461 total = $375 renewal + $16 HEAL-WA + $70 substance use disorder monitoring surcharge. Fees effective April 17, 2025 (WSR 25-07-080); all fees non-refundable.

WV.due: MD: staggered by last name. Physicians whose last names begin with A through L renew in even-numbered years; M through Z renew in odd-numbered years. The online renewal window opens in early May (May 6 in 2026) and closes promptly at 4:30 pm EDT on June 30; unrenewed licenses expire at 11:59 pm EDT on June 30. DO: license is valid for a term of 2 years and must be renewed by June 30 of the second year (W. Va. Code R. 24-1-4); the statute states renewal is biennial on or before July 1 (W. Va. Code 30-14-10), and the DO board requires the application and fees by June 30.
WV.fee: $400 (MD active status, 2-year renewal; inactive status is $150). DO renewal is also $400.00 plus a 2.25% processing fee when paying by credit card.

WI.board: Wisconsin Medical Examining Board (Department of Safety and Professional Services, DSPS)
WI.due: October 31 of each odd-numbered year, for all physicians statewide (Wis. Stat. 440.08(2)). The board states this applies even if the initial license was issued in the months just before the date: a license issued shortly before October 31 of an odd year still must be renewed by that date. Next renewal deadline: October 31, 2027.
WI.fee: $120 (Medicine and Surgery, MD or DO, 2-year renewal). Same $120 applies to the Compact (IMLC-issued) MD and DO credentials and to Administrative Medicine and Surgery licenses. Per the DSPS Renewal Dates and Fees schedule (RDAF, rev. 08/07/2025); DSPS's August 8, 2025 news release confirms the physician fee rose to $120 effective for applications opening in August 2025.

WY.due: Fixed date: all physician licenses must be renewed no later than June 30 of each calendar year, and each renewal carries the license through the next June 30 (Board rule, Ch. 1 Sec. 10; W.S. 33-26-305 requires annual lapse on a board-set date). First-time renewal depends on issue date: licenses issued July 1 through February 28/29 renew by the immediately following June 30; licenses issued March 1 through June 30 renew by June 30 of the next calendar year.
WY.fee: $155 (annual physician renewal, incl. administrative license, per Board fee schedule PDF effective January 30, 2023). EXCEPTION: the Board entirely waived the renewal fee for the 2026-2027 renewal year during its software conversion; paper renewals still pay a $25 paper processing fee. IMLC-issued licenses renewed via IMLCC paid $0 to Wyoming this year plus the IMLCC $25 processing fee.
